title: Fuel Tank and Lines — 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT
introduction:
Fuel delivery and fuel-vapor management are separate jobs. I keep them in separate mental trays: trouble containing vapor is not a verdict on fuel delivery, and a delivery complaint does not automatically implicate the vapor hardware. Even a reassuring fuel-gauge reading tells you about quantity, not whether the engine is getting the required supply.

This page’s diagnostic instruction is a referral to the applicable Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis manual. That manual is not included here, so equipment selection, setup, measurements and the branches that follow each result remain with that reference. This page does not provide a standalone diagnostic procedure.

items.name: Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual
items.detail: Use the diagnostic information applicable to the engine identified in this page’s title. Select test equipment and methods from that engine’s information.

edits.text: For fuel tank and line diagnosis, refer to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) manual and select the information applicable to this engine.
edits.why: Fuel-system pressure arrangements and testing requirements vary with the engine. Matching the reference keeps another configuration’s equipment or specifications from becoming an unsupported diagnostic shortcut.
